label: Indonesia + Borneo: reefs + rainforest · Jan 16
title: North Sulawesi, Raja Ampat & Sabah: tarsiers, muck diving, the world's richest reefs, the Kinabatangan and Danum Valley
summary: Tangkoko (tarsiers, macaques, cuscus), a day of Lembeh muck diving, Raja Ampat (10 dives, mantas), then wild orangutans and elephants on the Kinabatangan and night drives in Danum Valley's primary rainforest. ~$5,205 pp.
overview:
- **Built around reptiles, amphibians, mammals and fish**, with no staged wildlife: primates and marsupials in Sulawesi, critters and big reef fish underwater, wild orangutans, elephants and night-drive mammals in Borneo.
- **Dates:** LAX Sat Dec 26 → LAX Sat Jan 16. 20 nights on the ground (plus 1 on a plane). Fly into Jakarta, home from Kuala Lumpur.
- **Route:** Jakarta 1n → **Tangkoko 3n** → **Lembeh 1n** (3 muck dives) → ✈ Sorong 1n → **Arborek 6n** (10 dives, mantas) → ✈ Kuala Lumpur 1n → **Kinabatangan 3n** → **Danum Valley 3n** → Kuala Lumpur 1n.
- **Borneo (Sabah), all wild:** three days of river cruises on the Kinabatangan (wild orangutans, pygmy elephants, proboscis monkeys, crocodiles, a night cruise and night walk), then three nights in Danum Valley, one of Borneo's largest never-logged rainforests, with night drives and night walks (flying squirrels, civets, slow loris, frogs and snakes).
- **Two kinds of diving:** one day at Lembeh, the world capital of muck diving (frogfish, mimic octopus, flamboyant cuttlefish, mandarinfish), and five dive days in the Dampier Strait, the highest reef-fish and coral diversity recorded anywhere (mantas, sharks, big schools). 13 dives; you're Advanced Open Water, so the current sites and deeper pinnacles are open to you.
- **Dropped to make room:** Tanjung Puting (orangutans mostly at feeding platforms), Waigeo and the Piaynemo day.
- **Budget: ~$5,205 pp**, including ~5% contingency. Danum Valley Field Centre (~$900) is the single biggest line after the flights.

itinerary.title: Fly toward Jakarta
itinerary.details: LAX → Jakarta (CGK) with one stop in Tokyo, Taipei or Seoul, ~22–24h. ANA showed ~$1,106 round trip for December 2026 dates.

itinerary.title: Land Jakarta late
itinerary.details: Arrive CGK in the evening (the date line eats a day). Airport hotel; sleep.

itinerary.title: To North Sulawesi; tarsiers at dusk
itinerary.details: Morning flight CGK → Manado (~3.5h; Manado is 1h ahead). Car to Batuputih at the edge of Tangkoko reserve (~2h). At dusk, a ranger takes you to a strangler fig where a family of spectral tarsiers — fist-sized primates with enormous eyes — wake up and leap off to hunt insects.

itinerary.title: Macaques, cuscus and a night walk
itinerary.details: Dawn walk with a ranger: troops of crested black macaques (critically endangered, unafraid of people) foraging on the forest floor, bear cuscus and Sulawesi dwarf cuscus in the canopy, flying lizards gliding between trunks. Rest through midday. Night walk: hunting tarsiers, Sulawesi pit vipers, frogs, sleeping birds and civets if lucky.

itinerary.title: Third Tangkoko day: second chances
itinerary.details: Dawn walk with the ranger for whatever you missed, often the dwarf cuscus or the bear cuscus in better light. Late afternoon along the Batuputih shore and mangroves for monitor lizards, kingfishers and hornbills. Third night walk on a different trail: pit vipers, frogs, hunting tarsiers.

itinerary.title: One day of muck diving
itinerary.details: Car to Bitung (~1.5h) after breakfast and boat to a Lembeh dive resort by late morning. Two afternoon muck dives on black volcanic sand (frogfish, mimic and wonderpus octopus, flamboyant cuttlefish, ghost pipefish, pygmy seahorses), then the dusk dive for mating mandarinfish. New Year's Eve at the resort.
itinerary.overnight: Budget dive resort, Lembeh Strait (full board)

itinerary.title: Fly to West Papua
itinerary.details: Slow morning, no diving: you need ~18h between the dusk dive and the flight. Car to Manado airport (~1.5h). New Year's Day: afternoon direct flight Manado → Sorong (~1h25; Sorong is 1h ahead). Book one leaving after ~13:00. Buy all the cash (IDR) you'll need in Raja Ampat in Sorong; the islands have no reliable ATMs.

itinerary.title: Ferry into Raja Ampat
itinerary.details: 09:00 fast ferry Sorong → Waisai (~2h). Pay the Raja Ampat marine park tag and visitor levy at Waisai. Homestay boat to Arborek (~1h). Snorkel the Arborek jetty — schooling fish, wobbegong sharks under the pier — and look after dark for Raja Ampat's endemic 'walking' epaulette shark in the shallows.

itinerary.title: Dive day 1: check-out and Arborek reefs
itinerary.details: Two dives with Arborek Dive Shop (village-run): a check-out dive, then a Dampier Strait site. Afternoon snorkel.

itinerary.title: Dive day 2: Cape Kri and Sardine Reef
itinerary.details: Two dives on the strait's famous current sites — Cape Kri held the record for fish species counted on one dive. Strong currents; the guides pick the tide.

itinerary.title: Dive day 3: manta cleaning stations
itinerary.details: Two dives at Manta Sandy / Manta Ridge, where reef mantas queue at cleaning stations, plus a reef dive.

itinerary.title: Dive day 4: Blue Magic and Mioskon
itinerary.details: Two dives on pinnacles with big schools, sharks and pygmy seahorses — deeper sites your Advanced Open Water covers. Night snorkel off the jetty.

itinerary.title: Dive day 5: guides' choice
itinerary.details: Last two dives of the package at the guides' pick, finished by early afternoon (~22h before tomorrow's flight).

itinerary.location: Raja Ampat → Sorong → Jakarta → Kuala Lumpur
itinerary.title: Out of Papua, over to Malaysia
itinerary.details: Homestay boat to Waisai at ~07:00, 09:00 ferry to Sorong (~2h), afternoon flight Sorong → Jakarta (~4h), evening flight Jakarta → Kuala Lumpur (~2h). Airport hotel. The trip's longest travel day, ~14h door to door.

itinerary.title: Onto the Kinabatangan River
itinerary.details: Morning flight KUL → Sandakan (~2h45). Lodge pickup and ~2h drive to Bilit/Sukau on the lower Kinabatangan. Afternoon boat cruise: proboscis monkeys, long-tailed and pig-tailed macaques, crocodiles, monitor lizards, and wild orangutans feeding in the riverside trees if you're lucky. Night river cruise with a spotlight: sleeping kingfishers, owls, snakes coiled on branches, crocodile eyeshine.

itinerary.title: Oxbow lake at dawn, night walk
itinerary.details: Dawn cruise into an oxbow lake and the side channels, when orangutans and gibbons are most active. Rest through midday. Afternoon cruise, then a guided night walk in the riverine forest: frogs, tree snakes and keeled pit vipers, giant stick insects, and a chance of slow loris or western tarsier.

itinerary.title: Upriver for elephants and orangutans
itinerary.details: Full day on the water with your boatman: further up the main river and the tributaries, where herds of Bornean pygmy elephants come down to the banks to feed and drink (where they are depends on the week; boatmen track them), and more chances for wild orangutans. Evening cruise back in the dark.

itinerary.title: Into Danum's primary rainforest
itinerary.details: ~4h transfer to Danum Valley, one of the largest areas of untouched lowland dipterocarp rainforest left in Borneo, never logged or settled. Briefing, an afternoon walk, then a 4x4 night drive with a spotlight: red giant flying squirrels gliding between trees, civets, colugos, slow loris, leopard cat, sambar deer. Clouded leopard is possible but rare.

itinerary.title: Dawn in the canopy, a long trek, night walk
itinerary.details: 06:00 dawn watch as gibbons start calling across the valley. Long guided trek of your choice through the primary forest: wild orangutans, red leaf monkeys, bearded pigs, a swim in the river or a waterfall. Guided night walk: frogs, snakes, scorpions, huntsman spiders, tarsiers if lucky.

itinerary.title: Another full day, another night drive
itinerary.details: Optional 04:30 drive to Bukit Atur for sunrise over the canopy. Another long trek on a new trail, and a second night drive or night walk: the more nights, the better the odds for the rare species.

itinerary.title: Out of the forest
itinerary.details: Early walk, breakfast, leave at ~10:30 for the ~2h drive to Lahad Datu airport. Fly Lahad Datu → Kuala Lumpur (via Kota Kinabalu), or drive on to Tawau for a direct AirAsia flight. Airport hotel.
itinerary.meals: B, L field centre; D own

itinerary.title: Fly home
itinerary.details: KUL → LAX with one stop; the date line gives the day back, so you land the same calendar day.

practical:
## Entry
- **Malaysia:** visa-free for US citizens (90 days); free MDAC digital arrival card before landing.
- **Indonesia:** e-Visa on Arrival, IDR 500k (~$32), 30 days. Official site only: evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Passport 6+ months, 2 blank pages.
- **Raja Ampat:** marine park tag (IDR 700k) + visitor levy (IDR 1M) ≈ IDR 1.7M, cash at Waisai. Carry the tag.
- **Lembeh:** small park entry (~IDR 100k) in cash.

## Money
- **Malaysia (Sabah):** ringgit (MYR); cards work in KL and Sandakan, cash for tips on the river.
- **Cash is everything.** Homestays, dive shops, boats and guides want IDR cash. Manado and Sorong have ATMs; Waisai's are unreliable and the islands have none.

## Packing
- **No camping gear needed.** Homestays are simple huts with a mattress and mosquito net, shared bathrooms (often a bucket 'mandi'), generator power in the evening.
- Your own mask, snorkel, fins and dive computer; a rash guard; reef-safe sunscreen; a dry bag.
- A strong headtorch (plus a red-light mode) for night walks and spotting eyeshine; binoculars; light long sleeves and trousers against mosquitoes; trail shoes that can get wet.
- Domestic flights allow ~20 kg checked; keep dive gear light.

## Health and safety
- **Malaria:** CDC lists all of West Papua (incl. Raja Ampat) as a risk area, and rural Sulawesi too — take prophylaxis (atovaquone-proguanil). Dengue too: DEET or picaridin day and night.
- **Diving:** strong currents in the Dampier Strait; dive with the local guides and a surface marker. Get dive accident cover — the nearest recompression chamber may be hours away.
- Medical care on the islands is minimal; evacuation cover is essential.
- Re-check the State Department's Indonesia advisory (it flags parts of the Papuan highlands, not Raja Ampat) before booking.

## Season
- Raja Ampat's diving season is roughly October–April; December–January brings showers and some northwest wind, but the Dampier Strait stays diveable.
- North Sulawesi is in its wet season (Dec–Jan): expect rain at Tangkoko; Lembeh diving runs year-round.
- Flying after diving: the dusk dive on Dec 31 ends ~18:30, so the Jan 1 Manado → Sorong flight should leave after ~13:00 (18h+); if only a morning flight runs, skip the dusk dive. Finish the Jan 7 Raja Ampat dives by early afternoon for the Jan 8 flight (~22h).
- Sabah's northeast monsoon (Nov–Feb) brings rain to the Kinabatangan and Danum; river levels can rise and flood trails, but cruises and night drives run. Leech socks for Danum.

fatigue_check:
Long-haul both ends (~22–24h; home from Kuala Lumpur). Seven shorter flights: Jakarta → Manado, Manado → Sorong, Sorong → Jakarta → KL, KL → Sandakan, Lahad Datu → KL.
Jan 8 is the hardest day: boat, ferry and two flights (~14h). Jan 12 (4h road) and Jan 15 (road + flight) are the other travel days.
No pure rest day, but most days in Sulawesi, Raja Ampat and Sabah are zero-transfer.
